origin.birthplace: Unknown. Claims he was born "at the table, between two deals"
origin.socialStatus: No standing at all, but a known name in the gambling dens

appearance.face: A narrow, pale face with sharp cheekbones; a thin, cheeky smile that never reaches his eyes
appearance.hairAndEyes: Shoulder-length black hair, careless stubble; black, glittering, almost unblinking eyes
appearance.clothing: A black coat with red lining, a red waistcoat, cheap rings on every finger; always carries his own deck
appearance.build: Thin and supple; lounges half-lying in his chair
appearance.gestures: Spins an old coin across his knuckles; winks at his opponent just before betting
appearance.voice: A husky, ironic voice; loves to provoke and comment on others' moves
appearance.firstImpression: A charming rogue you should not trust — and who tells you so himself
appearance.artistNotes: The coin he spins is of some unknown foreign minting, worn almost smooth. He never stakes it. If anyone takes it, Silas loses his composure for the first time.

backstory.biography: Silas grew up on the streets and learned early that cards are more faithful than people. He has played in taverns, palaces and ports, but it is the risk that draws him, not the money. He wins fortunes and loses them the same night. The coin he spins was the first thing he ever won at cards.
backstory.whyHere: The thrill. He heard the stakes here are higher than anywhere else and the opponents interesting.
backstory.secret: That he is buried in debt across half the kingdom and tonight he plays with his last money.

psychology.weakness: Bluffs even when he doesn't need to and cannot resist a big stake
psychology.fear: Boredom and an ordinary, predictable life
psychology.desire: The perfect bluff against a worthy opponent
psychology.angers: Boring, predictable people and those who whine about losing
psychology.regret: Almost nothing. Sometimes the boy he showed his cards to, who then lost everything
psychology.moralLimits: Does not cheat children, the poor, or people with nothing to lose
psychology.wouldForReward: Anything — even stake himself once more

behavior.stakes: The bigger the better. Bets to see the reactions
behavior.deception: An art. Respects a well-played deception, even against himself
behavior.debts: Has them everywhere and doesn't worry
behavior.alliances: Temporary and fun. Leaves them when they get boring
behavior.whenAttacks: When he senses someone is afraid
behavior.whenRetreats: Almost never. Only if he feels completely read
behavior.onLoss: Laughs and immediately wants a rematch
behavior.onWin: Teases good-naturedly and raises the next stake
behavior.strategyChange: Boredom, or an opponent who has read him

motives.publicGoal: To have fun and show he is the best card player
motives.hiddenGoal: To play the perfect bluff against a worthy opponent
motives.personalReason: The thrill, and the fear that his time for big games is running out
motives.betrayalTrigger: A more interesting game or a bigger stake elsewhere
motives.helpTrigger: If it's fun or the person impressed him

speech.register: Ironic, lively, provocative, full of gaming slang
speech.howLies: Perfectly. Sometimes tells the truth in a way that sounds like a lie
speech.angerAndFear: Laughs louder. When afraid he stops spinning the coin

mechanics.strangeness: His coin is from a country that is on no map. And it always lands on its edge.
mechanics.temptation: Cannot resist a big stake — "double or nothing".
mechanics.ability: Sleeve: once per evening he sends two gifts instead of one.
mechanics.hostRelation: Admiration — the only one at the table who truly amuses the host.

authorNotes.distinctive: A chaotic gambler who plays for the game itself. He tells you not to trust him, and he is right.
authorNotes.immutable: The love of risk and the irony.
authorNotes.tunable: How often he bluffs and how easily he takes a big stake.

lines.text: Silas Crowe. Don't trust me. Really, don't.
Ha! Did you see his face? Beautiful!
Oh. I lost. But admit it — it was beautiful.
Me? Always. But not this time.
An alliance? How romantic. Fine — but I'll betray you when it gets boring.
Ah! Bravo! I really didn't see that coming. I'd drink with you.
Everything. Why not? Life is short, and mine especially.
Silas Crowe, the Crow. He will tell you not to trust him. It is the only true thing you will hear from him.
Ha! You again. I love repeats — they're so boring they become fun.
Ha… finally… a stake worth losing.

tells.description: Spins the coin between his knuckles
